title: Friedman Benda to Exhibit Work of Misha Kahn Whose Creations Adorned 'The Devil Wears Prada 2'
text: Friedman Benda to Exhibit Work of Misha Kahn Whose Creations Adorned ‘The Devil Wears Prada 2’ Misha Kahn's 'All Intensive Purposes' exhibit at Friedman Benda will showcase innovative designs in marble, metal, onyx, and plywood. ,” the experience was “wild. ” “I feel like a lot of objects I make are unplaceable. To see it in this movie was quite exciting. ” In reality, the Millennial artist’s designs, often fashioned in the form of oozing paste and gel, have been turning heads since he was featured in the Museum of Arts andand Mario Bellini. Four of Kahn’s works are currently on show at the Fondazione Dries Van Noten in Venice. Named “All Intensive Purposes,” the gallery will exhibit a new body of work whose structure is dictated by serious structure and form.Using materials from paper and cast metal to onyx, marble and plywood, Kahn transforms everyday fragments into technically rigorous objects that illustrate the intensity of “getting there. ”A visual journey complete with unexpected ridges and edges, cuts and nuances, the collection is, perhaps, a metaphor for the wonders and cruelty of life.“Life is serious and funny at the same time,” Kahn said in an interview with WWD, adding that expressions were crafted using both manual carving digital techniques. “I feel like we went so hard on this. Everything has both the ingenuity and the structure… and the relationship with what’s happening on the surface is so intense.” Pieces include a sprawling cast-metal dining table with a sculpted torn napkin complete with a discarded bite of food impaled with toothpicks, as well as a low table carved entirely from onyx forcing the stone to impersonate a much cruder construction. Other sculptural works, beleaguered shapes are crafted with Alpi plywood — embedded with colorful, multilaminar components embracing tree-forms.
